Chorus (system): chorus.gs_copies: Roland's eight macros, a line swept by one LFO, read at two outputs in opposite phase, fed back; laws GM 2's (rate, depth, feedback), the delay's chosen (0.2 ms a step); the wet share held as CC93's. To reverb / to delay, per-drum chorus sends, not yet
Controller matrix (GS 40 2x, GM2 09 0s): ctrlmatrix.py: GS's six sources (mod, bend, both aftertouches, the assignable CC1/CC2) and GM2's (channel and poly pressure, any CC) into amplitude (the fader's rows; an organ's gates), pitch (the bend row), cutoff (brightness at onset), LFO pitch depth (a sine on the bend row, so a held note's aftertouch vibrato moves), LFO amplitude depth (sidebands on rows of their own) and LFO rate -- measured in examples/ctrlmatrix_demo.py (Ben: phase 1 sounds good). The mod wheel's own vibrato (GS's 47-cent default) held out of files (TUNING_MOD_VIBRATO), LFO filter depth and live not yet
Delay (system): gsdelay.py: Roland's three taps, time table, ten macros, feedback through the center; CC94 (in a GS file) and the drum keys' sends; level laws chosen (linear over 127). Delay to reverb not yet a send of its own
EQ (system): the SC-88's two shelves at 200/400 Hz and 3/6 kHz, per part on/off, first-order (the order chosen)
Reverb (system): the macro picks one of our physical rooms by what it is for, small to large as Roland's run: Room 1-3 studio, chamber, a larger chamber; Hall 1 our concert hall, Hall 2 a grand one (Musikverein-scale); Plate an EMT 140 plate and Delay / Panning Delay a 100 ms echo, on the studio's walls (roomtail.device_ir) -- heard in examples/gs_reverb_demo.py (Ben: those all sound good). Its level and time scale the tail; CC91 a distance. Tokei was validated in the chamber under Hall 1 (now our hall: Ben chose the studio for it). Character, Pre-LPF, pre-delay and a per-drum reverb send not yet

3D Auto: the same, turning at its Speed; each note where its onset finds it; heard on our riff (Ben: "sound great")
3D Chorus: the chorus's outputs at 60 degrees, past the speakers; heard in its demo (Ben, 2026-10-21: these all sound great)
3D Delay: centre tap and two at 60 degrees; heard on our riff

Auto Pan: the same across the ears; heard on our riff
Auto Wah: efxfilter: a resonant LPF/BPF swept up (or down) from its Manual by its LFO, and opened by its Sens (the part's notes' envelope); heard on our riff and a Clav (Ben: "sounds great")
Bass Multi: compressor, OD, EQ, chorus/flanger, the 4x10 bass cabinet; heard on our riff (Ben: "sound great")
Cho -> Delay: the chorus and a delay tap (our passes run the delay first); heard on our riff (Ben: "sound great")
Cho -> Flanger: the chorus's copies, then a moving comb (efxfilter) on every row, the copies' too: in its order; heard on strings
Cho / Delay: TWO BRANCHES: the part's rows the chorus's, a copy on its virtual channel the delay's, each at its own Level and Pan (a gain across the ears; the chorus's copies keep its +-30 degree outputs); heard (Ben: "They all sound great")
Cho / Flanger: the chorus's branch and the flanger's, in parallel; heard (Ben: "They all sound great")
Clean Gt Multi 1: compressor, EQ, chorus/flanger and delay, as the guitar multis'; heard on our riff (Ben: "sound great")
Clean Gt Multi 2: an auto wah (efxfilter), the EQ, chorus/flanger and its delay; heard on a guitar
Compressor: efxbus: a level-following gain at the output's scale, 10-40 dB down at 8:1, attack 1-50 ms (chosen); heard on our guitar riff
DS -> Chorus: as OD -> Chorus with the distortion's gain; heard on our riff (Ben: "sound great")
DS -> Delay: as OD -> Delay with the distortion's gain; heard on our riff (Ben: "sound great")
DS -> Flanger: as OD -> Flanger with the distortion's gain; heard on our riff (Ben: "sound great")
Distortion: as Overdrive, with more gain; heard on storm_pro (kathie, SC-88Pro), its part 8 clean electric guitar at Drive 70 (Ben: sounds good)
EH -> Chorus: the chorus's copies, then the Enhancer on the part's bus (after them: the other way about); heard on an EP (Ben: "sounds great")
EH -> Delay: a delay tap, then the Enhancer's bus; heard on an EP
EH -> Flanger: the flanger, then the Enhancer's bus; heard on a guitar
Enhancer: efxbus: what lies above 2 kHz saturated, its harmonics mixed back by Mix; heard on an EP
FL -> Delay: the flanger and a delay tap; heard on our riff (Ben: "sound great")

Gate Reverb: efxbus: a noise burst Gate Time long convolved with the part -- Norm, Reverse, the two Sweeps; heard on Melodic Tom
Hexa Chorus: six voices spread in delay, depth and pan by its Dev parameters (0.5 ms a Pre Dly Dev step, chosen); heard in its demo (Ben, 2026-10-21: these all sound great)
Humanizer: efxfilter: three formants of its vowel (a/i/u/e/o), gliding at its Accel; its drive the valve's gain stage; heard on a Moog lead
Keyboard Multi: ring modulator (each partial's f +- Hz sidebands as gsdelay taps), EQ, pitch shifter, phaser, delay -- the series unrolled into a tap per path; heard on an EP
Limiter: efxbus: the compressor at its Threshold and Ratio, Release 10 ms-1 s (chosen); heard on our guitar riff
Lo-Fi 1: efxbus, the part's own bus: held to a lower rate, quantised to fewer bits (Type 1-9, chosen), its pre and post low-passes; heard on an EP and sysex_01 (Ben: "sounds great")

Mod Delay: the Stereo Delay with its modulation as the repeats' vibrato; heard on our riff
OD -> Chorus: the valve's gain stage and guitar cabinet, then the chorus (gs_copies); heard on our riff (Ben: "sound great")
OD -> Delay: the same with a gsdelay tap; its dry and effect by Bal; heard on our riff (Ben: "sound great")
OD -> Flanger: the same with the flanger; heard on our riff (Ben: "sound great")
OD / AutoWah: an OD branch beside an auto wah branch, its Sens the part's notes; heard (Ben: "They all sound great")
OD / Phaser: an OD branch beside a phaser branch (efxfilter); heard (Ben: "They all sound great")
OD / Rotary: an OD branch beside a Leslie branch (the voice's own valve in both); heard (Ben: "They all sound great")
OD1 / OD2: two OD branches, each the valve's gain stage and cabinet at its own drive, level and pan; heard (Ben: "They all sound great")
Overdrive: the OD a gain stage in front of the part's valve (tubeamp, its gains multiplying), its output makeup, the 1x12 cabinet; low/high gains after it. Amp Type (Small/BltIn/2-/3-Stack) one speaker for all; heard in the OD -> Chorus/Flanger/Delay demos (Ben, 2026-10-21: those sound great)
PH / AutoWah: a phaser branch beside an auto wah branch; heard (Ben: "They all sound great")
PH / Rotary: a phaser branch beside a Leslie branch; heard (Ben: "They all sound great")
Phaser: efxfilter: four all-passes at the swept corner, its resonance and mix, on every partial (the lobe kernel's filter_grid); heard on our riff
Reverb: efxbus: a decaying noise response per ear, its highs dying to HF Damp, six types by density, tail and early reflections (chosen); heard on an EP
Rhodes Multi: Enhancer (the bus), phaser (efxfilter), chorus/flanger, tremolo/pan; heard on an EP
Rotary: our Leslie at the type's rotor speeds, switched by Speed, Accl through our measured spin-ups, the rotors' levels -- RECORDED as Roland's is: two mics round the cabinet (Separate, 0-180 degrees), each to its speaker with its own swing and Doppler; heard on our Rhodes riff, mono and then with its two mics (Ben: "Those sound awesome", "Sounds great")
Rotary Multi: the Rotary with its OD (the valve) and EQ before the rotors; heard in its demo (Ben, 2026-10-21: those sound awesome)
Space D: chorus.gs_copies, two outputs half a turn apart, pre-delay and rate from Roland's tables, Balance the share; heard on SENSATIO
Spectrum: eight fixed peaking bands at the manual's frequencies, each partial's gain at its own; heard on a piano
Step Flanger: efxfilter: the flanger's comb, its line swept in steps; heard on our riff
Stereo Chorus: as Space D, its Phase and pre-filter (the LPF; its HPF not built); heard in its demo (Ben, 2026-10-21: these all sound great)
Stereo Delay: gsdelay: left and right taps each looping at its own period, feedback (cross for ping-pong), phase inversion, HF damping; heard on our riff (Ben: "They sound great")
Stereo Flanger: the chorus device with a flanger's swing, Roland's pre-delay and feedback, its outputs apart by its Phase; heard on our riff (Ben: "sound great")
Stereo-EQ: two shelves at their own corners and two peaking mids (gsefx.eq_gain), every partial; heard on sysex_01 (Ben: "These all sound great")
Tm Ctrl Delay: one tap at its time, placed by its pan (its time's glide under control not built); heard on our riff
Tremolo: the tremolo pass, Roland's five waves as Fourier series, the depth dipping the level; heard on our riff
Tremolo Chorus: the chorus and the tremolo pass (half depth, chosen); heard in its demo (Ben, 2026-10-21: these all sound great)

4.0: FITTED TO LEARMAN'S 1977 MARK I off the harp connector (jRhodes3d, CC BY-NC, measured only; examples/rhodes_fit.py), on what his EQ cancels -- the growl a harder layer adds, the hard attack's first 50 ms, the bark's fade, the decay (a tine sings 3-4x longer than we had it), the bass h1 BUILDING for seconds (F1 peaks 3.9 s in): the paper's own pickup (DAFx-17), a point tip over the magnet's frustum face on an arc, so a wide bass swing spikes each half cycle; each harmonic a sum of decaying layers, the swing's power series, at its true phase. Then voiced by ear: a forte that buzzes in the bass, mf untouched, and the buzz dying away faster than the tone (a wide swing damps faster); the register level even across the keyboard, as Gwazda's Wurlitzer measures (it had run 43 dB C2-C7 riding the swing). Ben, live: good and distinct from the Wurlitzer

6.0: FITTED TO VCSL'S HARPSICHORDS (CC0; examples/harpsi_fit.py): the English Normal and Lute sets and the Flemish High and Low, each stop measured as its difference from the 8' on one instrument, so the room drops out. A STRING BANK, like the piano: every choir on a key is present, each slightly apart in cents, stiffness and partial tuning, and the stops (the CC11 word, rated below) choose which the jacks pluck; a key lifts every damper, so the undrawn choirs ring through the bridge. The quill plucks at fixed force, so the comb never fills and there are no dynamics. The ladder and body over the whole band, partials to 16 kHz, the decay by band (log-rate error 0.96 -> 0.65), random partial phases (in phase they swept like a phaser, Ben), and the quill's catch before it slips (3.5-6 ms, measured). Ben: sounds great
